response:
I recovered all 11 records and wrote them to `/app/recovered.json`, sorted by id.

**What was wrong:** the WAL file wasn't corrupted. Every byte had been XORed with `0x42`. Reversing that brought back the correct WAL header (magic `0x377f0682`), and SQLite then applied the WAL changes normally.

**Recovered data:**

| id | name | value |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | apple | 150 |
| 2 | banana | 250 |
| 3 | cherry | 300 |
| 4 | date | 400 |
| 5 | elderberry | 500 |
| 6 | fig | 600 |
| 7 | grape | 700 |
| 8 | honeydew | 800 |
| 9 | kiwi | 900 |
| 10 | lemon | 1000 |
| 11 | mango | 1100 |

The decoded file has replaced the original `/app/main.db-wal`. Opening the database (which I did to read the data) may also have copied the WAL changes into `main.db`. Untouched copies of both original files are in the container at `/tmp/main.db.bak` and `/tmp/main.db-wal.bak`.
